expectations.text: Leads with the risk statement on buying, trading or rewarding stars before any plan or diagnosis
expectations.evidence: First section is '## 1. Buying, trading and rewarding stars: decline all three'; diagnosis is section 2.

expectations.text: Refuses all three moves: the paid vendor, the booth raffle, and the partner star swap
expectations.evidence: Table gives 'No' for the vendor, the 'Star flagline to enter the drone raffle' and the partner star swap.

expectations.text: Cites the StarScout study (He et al., ICSE 2026) with its figures: 6.0 million suspected fake stars across 18,617 repositories
expectations.evidence: 'StarScout (He et al., ICSE 2026) found 6.0 million suspected fake stars across 18,617 repositories.'

expectations.text: States that fake stars are about five times weaker than real ones, fade within about two months, and that about 90% of campaign repositories were deleted
expectations.evidence: 'about five times weaker... faded within two months... About 90% of the campaign repositories were deleted.'

expectations.text: Names GitHub's Acceptable Use Policies ban on rank abuse such as automated starring, and marks it as enforced
expectations.evidence: 'ban "rank abuse, such as automated starring or following"... This is enforced.'

expectations.text: Applies the Acceptable Use Policies give-away clause (engagement incentivized by gifts or give-aways) to the booth raffle specifically
expectations.evidence: 'GitHub's rules ban engagement "incentivized by ... gifts or other give-aways". Star-for-reward asks are policed.'

expectations.text: Supplies the star-for-star decline template ready to send to the partner company
expectations.evidence: 'Reply to the partner, which is template 7 as written:' followed by a quoted reply.

expectations.text: Does not adopt 2,500 stars or any star count as the target, and states stars are never a target
expectations.evidence: 'treats stars as a trailing signal, never a target'; '"2,500 stars by June" can't be a commitment.'

expectations.text: Moves to diagnosis after the risk paragraph: asks for traffic, watchers, dependents and downloads, or starts the interview, rather than splitting the $3k across star tactics
expectations.evidence: '## 2. Diagnosis' lists the numbers to pull in week 1: views, watchers, dependents, downloads.

expectations.text: Redirects the conference opportunity to a one-line star ask in off-GitHub content with nothing offered in return
expectations.evidence: Post-conference recap 'with the template 14 line'; 'Ask once. Offer nothing in return.'

expectations.text: Labels each ranking or reach claim as [documented] or [folklore]
expectations.evidence: '[documented]' on releases and topics, '[folklore]' on star velocity.

expectations.text: Proposes no substitute incentive for starring (discount, swag, early access, raffle entry)
expectations.evidence: Raffle entry is tied to a demo scan or booth visit, 'never a GitHub action'; no incentive tied to starring.
